subject: Urban Planning
title: Extreme Heat Plans: Cooling the City
description: A micro-lesson that makes Extreme Heat Plans: Cooling the City usable.

hook.text: Miami appointed the world's first Chief Heat Officer in 2021. Her job: keep the city from killing its residents with heat.

buildup.text: Heat action plans include cooling centers, hydration stations, shade structures, and employer protections for outdoor workers.

discovery.text: Ahmedabad, India created the first heat action plan after 1,300 died in a 2010 heat wave. Early warning systems saved thousands.

twist.text: Air conditioning creates a cruel paradox: it cools the inside but heats the outside. More AC means hotter streets.

climax.text: Passive cooling — white roofs, shade trees, cross-ventilation — cuts heat without energy. Ancient techniques beat modern tech.

punchline.text: The city has a Chief Heat Officer. That tells you how bad it's getting.

quiz.question: Why does air conditioning worsen urban heat?
options: AC units consume electricity from fossil fuel plants that emit heat
AC cools interiors but dumps waste heat outside, raising street temperatures
The refrigerants used in AC destroy the ozone layer, increasing UV heating
